title: OSIRIS-REx
fullName: Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, Security, Regolith Explorer
operator: University of Arizona (science lead), with spacecraft built by Lockheed Martin and managed by NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
summary: OSIRIS-REx was NASA's first mission to return a sample from an asteroid, targeting Bennu, a small, carbon-rich near-Earth asteroid chosen partly because its orbit makes it a slight long-term impact concern and worth understanding well. The mission's approach and mapping strategy drew on techniques ESA's Rosetta had used at comet 67P a few years earlier. OSIRIS-REx spent nearly two years surveying Bennu before attempting to collect a sample, discovering that the asteroid's surface behaved almost like a fluid, occasionally ejecting small particles into space.

instruments.name: OCAMS (OSIRIS-REx Camera Suite)
instruments.purpose: Wide-angle, close-range, and mapping cameras for surface imaging

instruments.name: OLA (OSIRIS-REx Laser Altimeter)
instruments.purpose: Built with the Canadian Space Agency to map Bennu's shape in fine detail

instruments.name: OVIRS (Visible and Infrared Spectrometer)
instruments.purpose: Identifies mineral and organic composition across the surface

instruments.name: TAGSAM (Touch-and-Go Sample Acquisition Mechanism)
instruments.purpose: Robotic arm that briefly touched the surface and released nitrogen gas to stir up and capture loose material

timeline.event: Departure from Bennu for the return cruise
Sample capsule lands in the Utah desert
Spacecraft renamed OSIRIS-APEX and retargeted toward asteroid Apophis

discoveries: Bennu is a loosely bound rubble pile with surprisingly low surface strength
Returned sample contained a diversity of organic molecules and hydrated minerals
Bennu occasionally ejects small particles from its surface for reasons still under study
notes: After dropping its sample capsule near the Great Salt Lake, the still-functional spacecraft was renamed OSIRIS-APEX and sent on an extended mission to study the asteroid Apophis following that asteroid's close 2029 approach to Earth.
